currentContext.business: TruAlt Bioenergy is a renewable energy company engaged in the manufacturing and sale of ethanol and allied bioenergy products, having commenced commercial operations in FY2022-23 and listed in October 2025. It operates five 1G ethanol distilleries in Karnataka on a multi-feed, year-round platform, produces Extra Neutral Alcohol, CO2 and fermented organic manure, and is building a Compressed Biogas business through two subsidiaries with strategic partners, alongside a downstream biofuel retail network. Customers span oil and gas companies, government agencies and state-owned enterprises, spirits producers and major consumer-goods companies; the entity reports NIL exports as a percentage of turnover.

currentContext.expansion: TruAlt's expansion runs on four tracks. (1) Ethanol: the installed base is five 1G distilleries in Karnataka aggregating 2000 KLPD, described as 'India's largest multi-feed & year-round Ethanol platform', of which 1300 KLPD is dual feed — Jamkhandi 500 KLPD (Dual Feed Integration 450 KLPD), Mudhol 700 KLPD (Dual Feed 550 KLPD), Khanapur 400 KLPD, Kerakalmatti 200 KLPD (Dual Feed 300 KLPD) and Badami 200 KLPD. The Board's Report records capitalisation of a grain-based plant to the extent of 1300 KLPD during the year. (2) Compressed BioGas: a six-plant build-out plus a further six identified. CBG Unit 1 at Jamkhandi (10.20 TPD, Leafiniti Bioenergy) is Operational; Unit 2 Mudhol (20.00 TPD) is in construction and expected operational by end of Q2 FY27; Unit 3 Kerakalmatti (20.00 TPD) and Unit 4 Badami (20.00 TPD) by end of Q3 FY27; Unit 5 Daund, Maharashtra (20.00 TPD) by end of Q4 FY27 — Units 2 to 5 sit in TruAlt Gas Pvt. Ltd. Units 6 to 11 (72.00 TPD aggregate) are with Leafiniti Bioenergy at locations identified in Karnataka & Maharashtra, where 'Lands for six units have been jointly identified.' Total CBG portfolio capacity is stated at 162.2 TPD, of which only 10.20 TPD is operational today. (3) SAF: a proposed 100 million litres/annum Sustainable Aviation Fuel plant. (4) Retail: 7 biofuel outlets operational with 4 more under construction, taking the network to 11 across Karnataka under Phase 1 of a stated 100-outlet rollout. On the rupee side, the only quantum stated is the capital-commitments named disclosure (contracts remaining to be executed on capital account, net of advances). Notably, the BRSR Principle 2 leadership table prints '-' for both R&D and Capex investments in technologies improving environmental and social impacts — a stated nil, not a blank.

risks.risk: Dependence on Oil Marketing Company offtake — OMCs sharply cut lifting despite the Company being production-ready
risks.note: The Board's Report states revenue 'was significantly impacted due to a sharp reduction in lifting by OMCs despite operational readiness and available production capacities'. This is a demand-side concentration risk the Company does not control: capacity and readiness were not the constraint, the buyer's lifting decision was. It is the single largest stated cause of the year's revenue shortfall.

risks.risk: Unexecuted ethanol allocation contingent on a court order — the pending 15 crore litre allocation following the Hon'ble Karnataka High Court order
risks.note: The Board's Report attributes part of the revenue impact to 'delays in implementation and execution relating to the pending 15 crore litre allocation following the Hon'ble Karnataka High Court order'. Volumes the Company is counting on for recovery sit behind judicial and administrative execution rather than commercial demand, and the timing of realisation is outside management's control.

risks.risk: Rising finance costs and leverage from the growth build-out
risks.note: The Board's Report states the fall in profit after tax was 'primarily attributable to an increase in finance costs arising from additional working capital facilities availed by the Company to support its business operations and also interest incurred on the account of grain-based plant established during the year', compounded by higher depreciation from capitalising the grain-based plant. Structurally: a capital-intensive expansion is being funded with debt while offtake is being withheld — the two risks compound. Credit standing is CRISIL A-/Stable (reaffirmed October 28, 2025) with India Ratings assigning IND A-/Stable / IND A2+ on bank loan facilities in April 2026.

risks.risk: Governance compliance failure — no Woman Independent Director on the Board through the reporting period
risks.note: A Secretarial Audit Report observation records that 'The Company failed to appoint the Woman Independent Director in compliance Regulation No. 17(1)a of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.' Management responds that the matter is receiving the highest priority and that it is in the advanced stage of finalizing a candidate, but the breach ran the full year in the Company's first year as a listed entity.

Listed by the Company as material issue 2 and classified as a pure Risk with NEGATIVE financial implications. Mitigation stated as advanced IT security systems, periodic vulnerability assessments and data encryption protocols. Relevant for an entity that has just become a listed, multi-site industrial operator with JV partners.

Material issues 4 and 5. Energy and Emissions Management is flagged as both Risk and Opportunity (positive and negative implications); Climate Strategy is flagged as a pure Risk with negative implications. For a biofuels producer this cuts both ways — the decarbonisation mandate is the demand driver, but the Company's own process emissions, feedstock footprint and carbon-intensity validation determine whether its product qualifies under tightening low-carbon fuel standards.

risks.risk: Human rights exposure with the governing policy not yet in place
risks.note: Material issue 12, a pure Risk with negative implications. The mitigation column concedes the Company 'is actively in the process of implementing a comprehensive Human Rights Policy' — i.e. the policy does not yet exist. The risks it names explicitly are forced labour, discrimination and unsafe working conditions, which is a live exposure given the Company's stated use of independent contractors overseeing on-site contract labour.

risks.risk: Employee health and safety across multi-site industrial and construction operations
risks.note: Material issue 13, a pure Risk with negative implications. The Company runs five distilleries plus five CBG plants under construction and a growing retail network; the Board's Report notes regular safety inspections and audits at 'all plants and project sites'. Construction-phase exposure is at its peak in FY27 with four CBG plants due for commissioning.

risks.risk: Sustainable value chain and supplier dependence
risks.note: Material issue 14, flagged as both Risk and Opportunity with positive and negative implications. The mitigation text speaks of 'building a reliable and responsible supply chain' and strengthening supplier relationships. Feedstock — sugarcane derivatives and grain — is the Company's dominant cost and its availability, pricing and sustainability credentials are set outside the Company.

Material issue 10, flagged as Risk and Opportunity with positive and negative implications. The Board's Report claims operations 'have been free from major work stoppages due to labour disputes or work cessation' and that attrition reflects stable retention, but no attrition figure is given in this routed text and the workforce includes contract labour engaged through independent contractors.

one-line thesis: FY26 PAT halved to INR 80 Cr (Standalone) due to OMC allocation disputes capping ethanol volumes at 34% of bid and higher depreciation from dual-feed capex, but FY27 offers a sharp rebound via court-mandated 15 Cr litre volume recovery and 16x CBG capacity scale-up. The transition to a multi-vertical biofuel platform (Ethanol+CBG+SAF+Retail) de-risks single-policy dependence, with near-term catalysts being the implementation of the Karnataka High Court order and commissioning of 9 new CBG plants.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,772 Cr (Consol, -7% YoY) due to volume constraints; EBITDA Margin: 20.98% (Consol, up from 19%); PAT: INR 96.86 Cr (Consol, down from INR 146.63 Cr) & INR 80.26 Cr (Standalone, down from INR 140 Cr); Order Book: 26 Cr litres (OMC) + 8 Cr litres (Private) + 15 Cr litres (Court Pending) + 6 Cr litres (ENA target); Net Debt: D/E 0.63 (Consol), robust liquidity (Current Ratio 1.71). One-offs: Depreciation surged 30% to INR 84 Cr due to capitalization of dual-feed conversion; Finance costs up 12% to INR 158 Cr.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Expect rebound in FY27 as 15 Cr litre court order implements (H1FY27) and CBG scales; Margin: CBG EBITDA >50-60%, Ethanol ~INR 67/litre realization; Order Inflow: Targeting 55 Cr litres total ethanol sales in FY27 pending court order; Capex/Commissioning: 9 new CBG plants (60 TPD Sumitomo + 72 TPD GAIL) by Q4FY27; SAF FID pending offtake agreements.
order book & pipeline: Ethanol: 24 Cr litres supplied in FY26; 26 Cr litres allotted FY27 (Public OMC); 8 Cr litres (Private OMC, 6.4 Cr pending lift); 15 Cr litres pending implementation per Karnataka HC order (Value INR 1,062 Cr). CBG: 10 TPD operational; 60 TPD (Sumitomo JV) & 72 TPD (GAIL JV) under construction for FY27 commissioning. Retail: 7 operational, 4 imminent, 76 identified.
segment / subsidiary detail: Ethanol: 24 Cr litres sold (FY26); Realization INR 67/litre; DDGS revenue INR 28 Cr; Dual-feed allows 200+ days operation on grain. CBG: 10 TPD plant at 85% utilization, EBITDA margin >55%; JV expansion to 162 TPD by FY27 end. SAF: MOU signed for 10 Cr litre plant in Andhra Pradesh; Honeywell UOP tech tie-up; targeting 20 Cr litre ethanol diversion. Retail: 7 outlets generating INR 105 Cr revenue, 5% EBITDA, zero capex model.
growth verticals / optionality: SAF vertical (10 Cr litre capacity) to absorb 20 Cr litres of ethanol production; Export potential to Japan/South Asia pending policy; Retail expansion to 87+ outlets (INR 1,000+ Cr revenue potential); CBG policy upgrade (Sampoorn) could lift gas price to INR 100/kg + INR 5 PLI.
margins & cost dynamics: Ethanol realization stable at INR 67/litre despite market oversupply; CBG margins robust at 55-60% (INR 84-85/kg selling price); DDGS realized INR 24/kg; Cost pressure from finance costs (+12%) and depreciation (+30%) due to completed capex cycle, expected to normalize as volumes ramp.
capex / expansion: Major capex cycle complete for dual-feed conversion (INR 400 Cr+ capitalized); Future capex minimal for ethanol; CBG expansion funded via JVs (Sumitomo/GAIL equity); Retail expansion on zero-capex franchise model.
capital allocation: Focus on debt reduction (D/E 0.63) and working capital for feedstock (INR 1,100 Cr cash/hand); JV route for CBG/SAF to preserve balance sheet; No dividend mentioned, reinvestment prioritized for volume ramp.
risks & watch-items: Policy/Regulatory: Delay in Karnataka HC order implementation by OMCs; SATAT policy changes; Volume Risk: OMC lifting delays (private OMCs lifted only 1.6/8 Cr litres); Market: Crude price volatility impacting retail/ena margins; Execution: Land acquisition delays for CBG (1 plant delayed).
management quality / tone: Resilient yet frustrated with OMC allocation mechanics; Confident on FY27 volume recovery via legal wins; Aggressive on diversification (SAF/CBG) to reduce government dependency; Transparent on one-time depreciation impacts.
non-obvious takeaways: The INR 460-500 Cr inventory buildup represents blocked revenue of ~INR 1,000 Cr that will flip to top-line immediately upon court order implementation; Retail strategy is a trojan horse to blend own ethanol at higher margins rather than pure trading; SAF plant location (Andhra) strategically chosen for proximity to refineries, airport, and port for export flexibility.

one-line thesis: FY26 PAT halved to INR 80 Cr (Standalone) due to OMC allocation disputes capping ethanol volumes at 34% of bid and higher depreciation from dual-feed capex, but FY27 offers a sharp rebound via court-mandated 15 Cr litre volume recovery and 16x CBG capacity scale-up. The transition to a multi-vertical biofuel platform (Ethanol+CBG+SAF+Retail) de-risks single-policy dependence, with near-term catalysts being the implementation of the Karnataka High Court order and commissioning of 9 new CBG plants.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,772 Cr (Consol, -7% YoY) due to volume constraints; EBITDA Margin: 20.98% (Consol, up from 19%); PAT: INR 96.86 Cr (Consol, down from INR 146.63 Cr) & INR 80.26 Cr (Standalone, down from INR 140 Cr); Order Book: 26 Cr litres (OMC) + 8 Cr litres (Private) + 15 Cr litres (Court Pending) + 6 Cr litres (ENA target); Net Debt: D/E 0.63 (Consol), robust liquidity (Current Ratio 1.71). One-offs: Depreciation surged 30% to INR 84 Cr due to capitalization of dual-feed conversion; Finance costs up 12% to INR 158 Cr.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Expect rebound in FY27 as 15 Cr litre court order implements (H1FY27) and CBG scales; Margin: CBG EBITDA >50-60%, Ethanol ~INR 67/litre realization; Order Inflow: Targeting 55 Cr litres total ethanol sales in FY27 pending court order; Capex/Commissioning: 9 new CBG plants (60 TPD Sumitomo + 72 TPD GAIL) by Q4FY27; SAF FID pending offtake agreements.
order book & pipeline: Ethanol: 24 Cr litres supplied in FY26; 26 Cr litres allotted FY27 (Public OMC); 8 Cr litres (Private OMC, 6.4 Cr pending lift); 15 Cr litres pending implementation per Karnataka HC order (Value INR 1,062 Cr). CBG: 10 TPD operational; 60 TPD (Sumitomo JV) & 72 TPD (GAIL JV) under construction for FY27 commissioning. Retail: 7 operational, 4 imminent, 76 identified.
segment / subsidiary detail: Ethanol: 24 Cr litres sold (FY26); Realization INR 67/litre; DDGS revenue INR 28 Cr; Dual-feed allows 200+ days operation on grain. CBG: 10 TPD plant at 85% utilization, EBITDA margin >55%; JV expansion to 162 TPD by FY27 end. SAF: MOU signed for 10 Cr litre plant in Andhra Pradesh; Honeywell UOP tech tie-up; targeting 20 Cr litre ethanol diversion. Retail: 7 outlets generating INR 105 Cr revenue, 5% EBITDA, zero capex model.
growth verticals / optionality: SAF vertical (10 Cr litre capacity) to absorb 20 Cr litres of ethanol production; Export potential to Japan/South Asia pending policy; Retail expansion to 87+ outlets (INR 1,000+ Cr revenue potential); CBG policy upgrade (Sampoorn) could lift gas price to INR 100/kg + INR 5 PLI.
margins & cost dynamics: Ethanol realization stable at INR 67/litre despite market oversupply; CBG margins robust at 55-60% (INR 84-85/kg selling price); DDGS realized INR 24/kg; Cost pressure from finance costs (+12%) and depreciation (+30%) due to completed capex cycle, expected to normalize as volumes ramp.
capex / expansion: Major capex cycle complete for dual-feed conversion (INR 400 Cr+ capitalized); Future capex minimal for ethanol; CBG expansion funded via JVs (Sumitomo/GAIL equity); Retail expansion on zero-capex franchise model.
capital allocation: Focus on debt reduction (D/E 0.63) and working capital for feedstock (INR 1,100 Cr cash/hand); JV route for CBG/SAF to preserve balance sheet; No dividend mentioned, reinvestment prioritized for volume ramp.
risks & watch-items: Policy/Regulatory: Delay in Karnataka HC order implementation by OMCs; SATAT policy changes; Volume Risk: OMC lifting delays (private OMCs lifted only 1.6/8 Cr litres); Market: Crude price volatility impacting retail/ena margins; Execution: Land acquisition delays for CBG (1 plant delayed).
management quality / tone: Resilient yet frustrated with OMC allocation mechanics; Confident on FY27 volume recovery via legal wins; Aggressive on diversification (SAF/CBG) to reduce government dependency; Transparent on one-time depreciation impacts.
non-obvious takeaways: The INR 460-500 Cr inventory buildup represents blocked revenue of ~INR 1,000 Cr that will flip to top-line immediately upon court order implementation; Retail strategy is a trojan horse to blend own ethanol at higher margins rather than pure trading; SAF plant location (Andhra) strategically chosen for proximity to refineries, airport, and port for export flexibility.
